stories.headline: United States Grand Prix 2026: Race start time in Austin, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.
stories.body:
Formula 1 heads to Texas for the United States Grand Prix, with the championship battle set to heat up at the Circuit of the Americas.

Max Verstappen claimed his second victory this season after winning the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time.

Kimi Antonelli continued to extend his lead in the title championship to 102 points from Mercedes teammate George Russell, and there is a mathematical chance he will be able to clinch the title in Austin.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 18th round.

All times in BST

Friday, October 23

Practice One: 6.30 p.m. - 7.30 p.m.

Practice Two: 10 p.m. - 11 p.m.

Saturday, October 24

Final Practice: 6.30 p.m. - 7.30 p.m.

Qualifying: 10 p.m. - 11 p.m.

Sunday, October 25

United States Grand Prix: 8 p.m. (GMT)

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the United States Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.

It's a mix of fast corners, long straights and has one of the steepest elevation climbs to Turn 1.

United States Grand Prix

Circuit: Circuit of the Americas; Austin, Texas

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2012

Lap record: 1:36.169, Charles Leclerc (2019)

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Most wins: Lewis Hamilton with six (2007, 2012, 2014-2017) Other winners from the current grid are Verstappen (2021-2023, 2025) and Leclerc (2024).

Most poles: Hamilton (2007, 2016-2018) is tied with Michael Schumacher (2000-2002, 2006) on four. Other pole sitters from the current grid are Verstappen (2021 and 2025), Carlos Sainz (2022), Leclerc (2023) and Lando Norris (2024).

Weather forecast

The weather for the United States Grand Prix is expected to be light rain with a gentle breeze throughout the course of the weekend, with highs of 32°C.

What happened last time out?
Verstappen edged out Norris to take an imperious pole position by 0.291 seconds.

The Red Bull driver dominated the race and posed as a serious threat to McLaren's Norris and Oscar Piastri in the drivers' championship.

Norris finished second and cut his lead to 14 points to Piastri in the standings, who finished fifth. Verstappen ended the weekend only 40 points behind Piastri with five races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli will be as focused as ever to claim his ninth victory of the season with one hand already on the drivers' championship trophy.

However, Mercedes are still working on how to best optimise its current upgrade package. Last time out in Singapore, the team ran Russell on the older specification, while Antonelli had the upgraded package.

Red Bull were labelled by rivals as the "team to beat" for the remaining six races of the season. There seems to be no stopping Verstappen, who has won the U.S. Grand Prix four times.

Don't count out Hamilton who holds the record for six wins around COTA and will be looking to get his seventh podium for Ferrari this season.

stories.headline: A global experiment: Can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or awards?
stories.summary: The Ballon d'Or awards are typically tough to predict, but can ESPN and our global resources do just that?
stories.body:
The destination of the Ballon d'Or is typically tough to predict. Just ask Real Madrid's Vinícius Júnior, who, in 2024, had spent weeks believing he would win the men's award only to learn hours ahead of the ceremony that it had gone to Manchester City midfielder Rodri instead.

This year, it is no less straightforward.

On the men's side, there are plenty of candidates: Teenager Lamine Yamal dazzled for Barcelona, Harry Kane scored more goals for Bayern Munich than he ever has before, Kylian Mbappé starred for Real Madrid, while the 2026 World Cup saw Lionel Messi and Rodri compete to be named the competition's best player (in the end, it went to Rodri).

And for the Ballon d'Or Féminin, Alexia Putellas is the favorite after captaining Barcelona to another quadruple, but she was far from the only world-class player on that team.

The winners for both will be revealed on Oct. 26 at a glitzy ceremony in London, alongside a number of other awards, but is there a way to gauge who will walk away with the prizes ahead of time?

The men's Ballon d'Or is decided by a group of 100 journalists, each from different countries, while the Ballon d'Or Feminin's voting roll is made up of 50 journalists from 50 different countries. We decided to replicate that voting with ESPN journalists stationed all over the world.

Here's how we did it:

Methodology:

ESPN has a global team of journalists in every corner of the globe. We asked 20 ESPN journalists from around the world -- one per country -- to submit a ballot.
We used the official Ballon d'Or shortlists.
We had each voter submit their top five for the Ballon d'Or and their top three for all other awards.
Like official awards, each first-place vote received 15 points, followed by 12 points for second, 10 points for third, eight points for fourth and six points for fifth.

So, in a global experiment, can ESPN predict the Ballon d'Or?

Jump to:

Ballon d'Or | Women's Ballon d'Or

Other awards

BALLON D'OR: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES

Lamine Yamal, Barcelona, RW

What our voters said:

Josué Utrilla, ESPN Guatemala reporter: "I believe that being a world champion -- while playing a key role in Spain's attack and enjoying excellent form with Barcelona in LaLiga -- demonstrates the talent he possesses at such a young age (19) and has earned him a place among football's biggest stars."

Harry Kane, Bayern Munich, ST

What our voters said:
Tom Hamilton, ESPN UK senior writer: "Okay, he didn't win the World Cup, or the Champions League, but Kane's year is unsurpassed. He scored 73 goals in 65 matches across the England national team and Bayern. It's a freakish record, the like of which we'll never see again. Let's park sentimentality and aesthetic-influenced bias; this award rewards individual brilliance."

Thijs Zwagerman, ESPN NL reporter: "Despite scoring goals at an extraordinary rate for years, Kane still does not receive the full recognition he deserves on the international stage. His qualities extend far beyond his remarkable goal-scoring record. He possesses the rare ability for a striker to drop deep, influence the game from a deeper position and operate like a playmaker as well. While Kane has yet to win the Champions League or the World Cup, that does not diminish his individual brilliance. In my view, he was still the best player in the world on an individual level."

Lionel Messi, Inter Miami CF, FW

What our voters said:
Anirudh Menon, ESPN India editor: "If this award is to be given to the best footballer on the planet, there can only be one answer. He may be 39 years old; he may even be playing in Major League Soccer (where he did win the MLS Cup and topped almost every attacking chart in the league), but the 2026 World Cup showed just how vast the gulf between Messi and everyone else remains. When he turns it on, there isn't anyone close. Give him his ninth Ballon d'Or already."

Teo Coquet, ESPN Argentina reporter: "I choose him because of his attacking influence and ability to remain decisive on the international stage. His performance for Argentina at the World Cup is also a key factor in my evaluation. At 39 years old, he has played one of the best World Cups of his career."

Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid, ST

What our voters said:

Omar Flores, ESPN Mexico reporter: "Mbappé was the leading scorer across every competition he played in during the 2025-26 season, topping the charts in both the UEFA Champions League and Spain's LaLiga. At the World Cup, the France star scored 10 goals and became the tournament's all-time leading scorer (22 goals). Although he was unable to help his team advance beyond the semifinals, he remains one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d'Or. "

Carlos Valdez, ESPN Colombia reporter: "I would put Mbappé first because of his extraordinary ability to make the difference at the highest level. His pace, finishing, consistency and capacity to deliver in decisive moments make him one of the most influential players in world football. His goal-scoring achievements across the league, Champions League and World Cup further strengthen his case. For me, the Ballon d'Or should recognize not only outstanding numbers, but also a player's ability to change the course of a game, and Mbappé embodies that quality."

Fabián Ruiz, Paris Saint-Germain, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain reporter: "If we forget about the cameras, the spotlights, the commercial interests, and all the pomp that increasingly accompanies the business of football, then Ruiz should win the Ballon d'Or. I have no doubt about it. Why? It's simple. He was an undisputed and fundamental player for PSG's repeated Champions League title success last season, and was equally fundamental for Luis de la Fuente's victorious Spain side at the 2026 World Cup when Pedri wasn't at his best in midfield. Ruiz won it all over the past 12 months and was a standout player. He lacks marketing appeal, which will work against him, but he would be a deserving winner."

Rodri, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Jean Beausejour, ESPN Chile analyst: "In a World Cup year, winning the tournament carries enormous weight. Rodri had a tremendous influence on Spain's performances on football's biggest stage. Spain's ability to dominate matches, control the tempo and impose their style of play against different opponents was largely down to Rodri's intelligence, positioning and exceptional ability to dictate the game. His influence went far beyond individual statistics, making him, in my opinion, the most deserving candidate for the Ballon d'Or."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: HARRY KANE

In a symbol of how divisive the men's Ballon d'Or race is, Kane received half of the first-place votes but only one of the other 10 voters put him second. Perhaps the biggest surprise was the large snubbing of Yamal, who received just a single No. 1 vote.

This was a two-horse race and, as ESPN writer Bill Connelly wrote earlier this month: "Kane played eight more matches and over 600 more minutes than Yamal -- which is to say, he stayed healthier than a player 14 years his junior -- and he produced 81 combined goals and assists, a full 36 more than Yamal."

There is a slice of history on offer for Kane, too: Kane would be just the fifth Englishman to cradle the golden trophy, alongside Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.

BALLON D'OR FEMININE: PLAYERS WHO GOT 1ST-PLACE VOTES
Alexia Putellas, London City Lionesses, AM

What our voters said:

Leonard Solms, ESPN Africa reporter: "In her final season at Barcelona, midfield maestro Putellas not only captained Barcelona to the Liga F, UEFA Women's Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de España trophies -- but also scored 20 goals and assisted 14 in 43 games. Capable of filling multiple roles in the team, Putellas is the kind of player any manager would love to have 11 of, and her brilliance should not be taken for granted."

Marissa Lordanic, ESPN Australia editor: "Putellas was once again invaluable across multiple competitions. The epitome of a big-game player, she ensured Barcelona's trophy case continued to grow before she tested herself in a new league."

Ewa Pajor, Barcelona, ST

What our voters said:

Gustavo Hofman, ESPN Brasil reporter: "Pajor combined outstanding individual production with collective success and delivered when it mattered most. She recorded 34 goals and eight assists in 46 appearances for club and country, helping Barcelona win the Champions League, Liga F, Copa de la Reina and Spanish Super Cup. Her intelligent movement and clinical finishing gave Barcelona a cutting edge throughout the season, but her Champions League performances ultimately put her ahead of the competition: she finished as the tournament's top scorer with 11 goals and scored twice in the 4-0 victory over OL Lyonnes in the final."

Ed Dove, ESPN Africa reporter: "In recent years, Pajor's performances haven't always been rewarded with the silverware and honors one might expect. That changed last term, where she was a key influence -- and a major goal threat -- in Barcelona's historic Quadruple-winning campaign. A genuine big-game player, she scored 33 across all competitions, including 11 in the Champions League, where she struck in every knockout round Barca played in before netting twice in a one-sided final victory over OL Lyonnes. Pajor may have scored fewer than she did during his remarkable debut season at Barca, but after overcoming the UWCL final defeat by Arsenal in 2025, she deserves the individual recognition here."

Temwa Chawinga, Kansas City Current, FW

What our voters said:

Jeff Kassouf, ESPN (US) reporter: "No player changes a game like Chawinga. She can create chances on her own in one-vs.-one situations from literally inside her own half on the counter attack, and is a sharp goal scorer. Scoring 20 goals in the NWSL and then following that up with 15 the next season is dominant form at a world-class level. And she does it for club and country, having helped lowly Malawi to the 2027 World Cup. This time next year, more international opponents will know the fear of having Chawinga run at their defense."

Patri Guijarro, Barcelona, CM

What our voters said:

Moises Llorens, ESPN Spain: "The backbone of Barcelona's women's team and an excellent midfielder who makes runs from the second line. Other players usually steal the spotlight, but her talent is unquestionable. She makes the rest of the team shine."

ESPN'S PREDICTED WINNER: ALEXIA PUTELLAS
This result is not a surprise. Putellas is the clear favourite for the award, and our voters agreed.

Putellas enjoyed a dream end to her 14-year Barcelona career last season, captaining the club to a second Quadruple in three years, including lifting the Women's Champions League, before she moved to captain London City Lionesses, who are now third in the Women's Super League after five games.

Should Putellas actually win, she would earn her third Ballon d'Or award, joining former Barcelona teammate Aitana Bonmatí as its most frequent recipient.

stories.headline: João Pedro: I told Cole Palmer 'I didn't want to take his spot' at Chelsea
stories.summary: João Pedro has said that a "friendship was born" when he assured Cole Palmer that he wasn't coming to Chelsea to steal his place in the team.
stories.body:
João Pedro has said that a "friendship was born" when he assured Cole Palmer that he wasn't coming to Chelsea to steal his place in the team.

João Pedro was named Chelsea's Player of the Season in 2025-26 after recording 20 goals and nine assists in 50 appearances, following his move to the Blues from Brighton in 2025.

This season under Xabi Alonso's leadership, João Pedro and England pair Palmer and Morgan Rogers have formed a fearsome attacking trio.

João Pedro told ESPN that the good atmosphere in the Chelsea dressing room has helped his evolution into a No. 9: "I think so, yes -- especially here at Chelsea, where I'm surrounded by world-class players like Cole Palmer, Reece [James] and Moses Caicedo.

"I think my adjustment went well because it had been a while since there was a No. 9 here. Ever since my time at Brighton, I'd been keeping an eye on that spot -- even when I played against them, I knew it could be an opportunity for me -- and, thank God, when I arrived, Cole was a great friend to me; he reached out to me and talked to me.

"I told him I was coming to help, that I didn't want to take his spot -- nothing like that.

"And that's where a friendship was born that we carry on both on and off the field. And I think what helps me a lot -- and now Morgan [Rogers] too -- is that we have a really great friendship on and off the field; we're always joking around.

"I think that's why -- I think the players were really friendly toward me when I arrived; they welcomed me with open arms, wanted to help me, and were willing to do so -- so I think that's why I adapted so well."

- Jordan Henderson, the Premier League's oldest player, is becoming undroppable for Chelsea

- Chelsea's Emi Martínez has jaw surgery, will be 'back in a few weeks'

- Jordan Henderson not giving up on England after Chelsea revitalisation

Despite his strong start in London last season, João Pedro, 25, was surprisingly left out of Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad by Carlo Ancelotti.

In just six Premier League appearances this campaign, he has five goals and three assists.

"At Chelsea I feel very comfortable," the Brazilian said. "It's a different season, with a coach who gives me a lot of confidence, and I think that's a big part of my performance so far this season."

Chelsea, fourth in the Premier League, appear to be benefitting from Alonso's preferred tactical 3-4-2-1 formation and so is João Pedro.

"I think it does make it easier," he said. "I have Cole and Morgan there to help me, to feed me the passes -- you can see that the start of the season has been really good. So I think it's going to be a really good season for us."

João Pedro has come a long way during his time in England, after starting at Watford, then joining Brighton and eventually moving to Chelsea.

A pivotal moment came, he said, when he played at Watford from 2020 until 2023: "I think that for my success here, the decisive moment was when Watford was relegated to the second division [in May 2022] and I stayed anyway.

"I worked hard and proved that I could overcome that challenge. Because a lot of the time, we Brazilian players come to Europe thinking everything will be a bed of roses, but sometimes that's not how it goes... and we end up giving up, but I think that was the moment when I said to myself: 'No, I came here, and I'm going to succeed here.'

"And thank God, today I'm at Chelsea.

"I have a phrase tattooed on me that says: 'Just as there are bad moments, there will be happy ones too.' I try not to focus on the past... what's done is done."

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

- Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson, and the Press Association, contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Bears' Santos gets redemption with game-sealing FG after 'annoying' miss vs. Pats
stories.summary: Bears kicker Cairo Santos walked away from Thursday's win over the Patriots a savior despite being haunted by a fourth-quarter miss.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- Bears kicker Cairo Santos walked away from Chicago's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots on Thursday night a savior after booting a career-long 58-yard field goal to seal the victory. But it was the miss he had one drive prior that dampened his demeanor postgame.

"The misses annoy me," Santos said.

On the Bears' first drive of the fourth quarter, Santos' 53-yard attempt hit the right upright and prevented Chicago from taking a two-score lead to cap off a 13-play drive that spanned 6 minutes, 56 seconds.

He got redemption on the Bears' next possession and essentially iced the game by extending Chicago's lead to nine. Santos struggled to express much joy postgame, focusing more on the opportunity he squandered versus the one that led Chicago to its fifth win of the season.

"I'm having a hard time celebrating these moments and I shouldn't act this way, but I just feel like I'm hitting the ball way too good to have these misses happen," Santos said. "Even though they're from 50-plus, I've been making them all the time."

The 34-year-old kicker went 3-for-4 on field goals and made all three of his extra points against the Patriots. Santos gave the Bears their first points when he made a 43-yard field goal on the game's opening drive and added a 31-yarder in the second quarter.

Despite Santos' miss, coach Ben Johnson didn't lose confidence in his kicker. On the following drive in the fourth quarter, the Bears' offense stalled when Caleb Williams took a 10-yard sack on third down at the Patriots' 30-yard line.

Santos said that Johnson had initially planned to send the punt team out on fourth down but changed course during an injury timeout for Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore, who got hurt while sacking Williams.

"I was talking to [special teams coordinator Richard Hightower] HT that I felt good about the line," Santos said. "And then Ben asked, 'Does he want it?' And I heard it and I told HT, 'I want it.' And then Ben said he wants it. I'm thankful that Ben trusts me on that."

Given the situation, Johnson had no qualms about giving Santos another shot.

"One, we felt good about being inside that line, and two, we asked him, he said, 'Absolutely, I need redemption because I missed one earlier,'" Johnson said. "He came through for us in a big way."

Santos was mobbed by teammates in celebration after his 58-yard attempt cleared the uprights in the south end zone. He is now 11-for-15 on field goal tries this season, including 3-for-5 from 50-plus yards.

Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, who coached Santos in Tennessee in 2019, was not surprised that his former kicker came through in a critical situation.

"I think the last field goal Cairo missed was when he kicked for the Titans, so I don't think he has missed one since then," Vrabel said. "He missed one earlier in the game, but we always joke about it. I'm really proud of what he's done. I didn't want him to make it tonight, but a former guy that we coached and Caleb is going to make some plays."

Santos' previous career long went 55 yards. Had he missed his fourth attempt Thursday, the Patriots would have just under two minutes to reach the end zone while trailing by six.

Instead, Santos connected on the third-longest field goal in Soldier Field history.

"He's consistent, and that's all you can ask for as a man," Williams said. "As a human, it's the hardest thing to do. And so that's who he is. And then from there, he has confidence in himself. He knows that we have confidence in him. He knows his quarterback has confidence in him. I think that only builds his confidence in himself, his routine, his everything. He's been doing it for a while. So, excited for him. Excited to be able to hit that for us as a team. It was big for us."

Santos entered Week 7 having missed two field goals in back-to-back games. He attempted a 56-yarder in Atlanta on Sunday that went wide left and missed a 43-yarder in Green Bay that also sailed left of the uprights.

"It's just been annoying to leave one play I feel like every game," Santos said. "And then I feel like I'm really performing well during the week, pregame warmups, kicking the ball really well. But just been so annoying to just leave that one play every game for my team but have a chance to have their back at the end with a career long. That was awesome."

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: Stephen Vogt back to Guardians in '27, shuns Mariners rumors
stories.summary: Guardians manager Stephen Vogt dispelled speculation about his future, saying he'll return next season to chase an elusive World Series title.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- Guardians manager Stephen Vogt dispelled speculation about his future, saying he'll return to the club next season to chase an elusive World Series title.

"I'm here," Vogt said at a news conference Thursday. "I'm coming back."

Vogt has led the Guardians to a division crown in each of his three seasons, He has twice been named American League Manager of the Year. With the Seattle Mariners' managerial spot open, there had been rumblings about Vogt possibly leaving in order to be closer to his family's home in Olympia, Washington.

However, the 41-year-old Vogt said he has not been contacted by the Mariners, who fired Dan Wilson last month following a disappointing 76-86 season.

Vogt spent one season as Seattle's bullpen coach in 2023 before being hired by Cleveland and that relationship helped fuel theories about a departure.

"I'll be in Cleveland," Vogt said three days after the Guardians were eliminated in the American League Championship Series by Tampa Bay. "I have not gotten a phone call."

While Vogt is adamant he's staying, it remains possible the Mariners could call the Guardians with a trade offer. Though rare, trades involving managers in Major League Baseball are not unprecedented, with the most recent one involving John Farrell going from Boston to Toronto in 2012.

Guardians president of baseball operations Chris Antonetti was asked about a potential pitch from the Mariners.

"I have every expectation that Voter is going to manage here for a really long time," Antonetti said, using Vogt's nickname. "We don't have any interest in Voter managing anywhere else."

Vogt signed a multiyear contract extension with Cleveland following the 2024 season. That deal was never made public and the club's secrecy about the contract's terms might have played a part in the rumors about a move.

A father of three, Vogt has been open about the difficulty of being away from his loved ones over an extended period. His wife, Alyssa, and their kids join him in the summer, but the months apart are hard on him.

"It's not just since I've been here. This has been my whole playing career," said Vogt, who played with six teams from 2012 to 2022. "It's very difficult living on the other side of the country, especially with my kids' age. My daughter's in high school, my boys are starting to get older, their activities are going up, so it's more challenging for them to get out here on a whim.

"But my wife's incredible and she reminds me every day that I'm where I'm supposed to be and I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing. And she jokes, 'We don't need you anyway.' Not joking. It's the worst part of my job."

As for the job he did this season with Cleveland, Vogt deserves praise.

One of the league's youngest teams, the Guardians regrouped from a sluggish first half and, bolstered by several trade deadline acquisitions, caught Chicago and won the division. They then rallied from an 0-2 deficit to stun the White Sox in the AL Division Series.

Cleveland's magic disappeared against the Rays, extending baseball's current longest World Series drought to 78 years.

Through it all, Vogt believed the '26 Guardians would prevail.

"There was a belief that we were just going to do it," he said. "We were never out of it. It wasn't like '25 where we did this historical comeback, needed a bunch of help. We controlled our destiny and we went out and grabbed it and took it."

In other Guardians news, pitching coach Carl Willis, 65, will return for a 15th season with Cleveland (over two stints).

"He's given a ton to this organization and is insanely competitive," Antonetti said of Willis, who has helped develop five Cy Young winners during his career. "He really wants to win a World Series in Cleveland for Cleveland."

Also, Vogt said the curious lack of postseason use for starter Tanner Bibee was because the team wanted to lean on its left-handed pitchers. Vogt said he spoke with an "upset" Bibee before Game 6 of the ALCS.

"We ended up talking about a lot more than just baseball and had a similar conversation in his exit interview," Vogt said. "It was very candid. It was very open. He spoke his mind and we gave him our reasoning. Tanner's going to be a huge part of this team for a long time and I'm really excited about that."

stories.headline: UFC 333 preview and picks for featherweight, men's bantamweight titles
stories.summary: Check out the matchups and expert predictions for both championship fights at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi.
stories.body:
How does a fighter know when to stop when they're fighting well?

It's a question that, unfortunately, rarely gets answered in MMA. For every athlete who retires from the sport on their own terms, there are at least two athletes being retired by the sport. It is rare for a fighter to go out on a win, and infinitely rare for a fighter to go out on top.

UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski (28-4) is starting to look that question in the face. Volkanovski will look to defend his title at UFC 333 on Saturday against 32-year-old Movsar Evloev (20-0) in Abu Dhabi, UAE. Volkanovski, 38, already is defying the rules of Father Time. In April 2025, he became the first fighter older than 35 to win a UFC championship belt in a weight class under 170 pounds. He defended that title in January against 31-year-old Diego Lopes.

In the past, Volkanovski has been dismissive, even comedic, of his age, starring in self-deprecating "Old Man Volk" skits on the internet. Ahead of UFC 333, however, he's been discussing age far more seriously, saying that any fight moving forward could be his last.

"There's a reason this is not often done," Volkanovski told ESPN. "I will bring up [my age], because I think it adds to the story. A lot of people are thinking about it. The young, undefeated guy -- facing the old, 38-year-old."

Evloev, of Russia, is one of the most proven title challengers in featherweight division history, with a perfect 10-0 record inside the Octagon, but he hasn't finished a single UFC opponent. He is a slight underdog against Volkanovski, according to DraftKings -- a credit to how good Volkanovski has looked, as well as lingering doubts on Evloev's ceiling.

Volkanovski, a two-time champion who suffered back-to-back knockout losses to Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria before regaining his title in 2025, told ESPN he believes he will actually look better than ever on Saturday, due to Evloev's style. The undefeated challenger is known primarily as a position-focused grappler, who might struggle to match Volkanovski's striking and scrambling ability.

"His style is a perfect matchup for me, I truly believe that," Volkanovski said. "I'm not delusional, saying I'm the best I've ever been at age 38. I'm not in my prime. But stylistically, I think you guys will be saying, 'I swear this is the best Volk we've ever seen.'"

Even if that is the case, odds say Volkanovski is tempting fate with every performance from this point forward. Male UFC fighters 38 and older have won 37% of their bouts all time, according to ESPN Research. Volkanovski has acknowledged as much and even proposed a "sendoff" title fight against 37-year-old lightweight champion Justin Gaethje next, after which they would both retire.

Volkanovski has stated he's taking it one fight at a time, but he is talking about retirement now, which shows he understands the decision is in front of him.

"One hundred percent, if I notice I'm slowing down or I'm taking more damage, [I'll retire]," Volkanovski said. "I said that before my last fight, too. A lot of people look at me saying that and say, 'Look how he's talking, his head isn't in it.' I'm just real and I'm honest. I said it before my last fight, and what happened? I went out there and made it look easy."

More storylines to watch

Dvalishvili looks to prove the last fight was an outlier
Merab Dvalishvili attempted to make history at the end of 2025, when he fought Petr Yan in his fourth men's bantamweight title defense of the calendar year. The feat has never been accomplished -- or even attempted -- and it proved to be too much as Dvalishvili lost a five-round decision. He later revealed he went into the bout with a significant knee injury and had a terrible camp. Dvalishvili (21-5) will try to recapture his title against Yan (20-5) in the UFC 333 co-main event.

Although he's admitted to tough circumstances around their last meeting, Dvalishvili has also said he doesn't regret pursuing UFC history and won't use those circumstances as an excuse, crediting Yan for the victory.

But the fighters' shared history has obviously raised the stakes for this Saturday. Dvalishvili and Yan have met twice, with Dvalishvili dominating their first meeting in March 2023. If Yan wins the trilogy, against a much fresher version of Dvalishvili than he saw in December, it could push Dvalishvili toward the back of the line for another title shot.

Not the last chance, but kind of the last chance
Not to put unnecessary pressure onto Aaron Pico's shoulders, but the truth is that any type of loss to Losene Keita -- a promising talent who is only 1-1 in the UFC -- would have heavy, long-lasting implications.

Pico, 30, has won 10 of his past 12 fights, but this is still a crossroads. He's been viewed as championship material since before his professional MMA debut, but has endured violent, memorable setbacks at various points in his career, including a spinning back elbow knockout loss to Lerone Murphy in his UFC debut 14 months ago. There is still massive potential in Pico, and he had an impressive bounce-back win against Patricio Pitbull in April, but he's in a risky position this weekend. He faces a dangerous but relatively unknown opponent in Keita after his original opponent, Arnold Allen, was forced off the card. Saturday's outcome will go a long way in determining how matchmakers and fans view him moving forward.

Coaches' questions and predictions for the title fights

Can Evloev significantly control Volkanovski on the ground?
Evloev is good everywhere, but Volkanovski has such an ability to game plan and show up in the big moments. Evloev is super big and strong. He has good standup, great transitions and ground control. But Volkanovski was able to get up after being taken down by Islam Makhachev. Are we just gonna forget that? Islam is now a welterweight. Volkanovski is so intelligent and so good at finding ways to exploit guys. His fight IQ is as good as anyone I've ever watched. He showed it against Lopes in their rematch in January. If Evloev cannot control Volk on the ground for long periods of time, Volkanovski will win a decision. And with the modern emphasis on damage when it comes to scoring, judges don't want to see you unsuccessfully try to hold someone down. Volkanovski by decision. -- Sayif Saud, Fortis MMA

Will age catch up to Volkanovski?
The biggest X factor is that unknown: At what point does Volkanovski's age slow him down? He's fighting one of the purest wrestlers/grapplers in the UFC in Evloev. I could see Evloev trying to prove he can stand with Volkanovski at times and win over the UFC, but I don't think that would be his smartest decision. Personally, I believe that "Old Man Volk" still has it. He's proven time and again he's going to win those key wrestling scrambles, and I believe he'll end up catching Movsar. It will be a grinder of a fight, but Volkanovski's experience being in there with bigger, stronger guys like Islam will pay off. Volkanovski by TKO. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Can Dvavishvili hurt Yan with his hands?
We know that Yan has the physicality to compete with Merab's wrestling. He didn't avoid the takedown in their last fight -- he actually got more takedowns than Merab. That's a fact. And Yan on the feet is so dangerous, you have to give his standup the edge. If he comes in in great shape and can counter-wrestle and have the same physicality he did in December, he can win. The biggest technical question is whether Merab can create enough offense to get inside and hurt Yan with his hands. If the wrestling gets shut down, can he create offense? If Merab can hurt Yan on the feet, that changes the whole fight and throws it in favor of Merab. I've got Yan winning by a slight edge. -- Saud

Who will control the resets?
Yan needs to control the range, punish Merab's entries and continually invest in the body. He needs to establish the center and force Merab to initiate his wrestling from a distance, and intersect those entries with straight punches, body shots and uppercuts. I'd like to see him keep that lead arm frame, to establish his underhooks right away with his wrestling defense. He doesn't need to eliminate the takedown attempt, but he does need to make Merab pay for every failed attempt. Merab, meanwhile, has to weaponize pace, create chaos and disrupt Yan's comfort. He has to chain together multiple takedown attempts, so that even failed attempts affect Yan's rhythm. Who will control the resets? Merab thrives when one attack becomes three or four; Yan thrives when he's able to reset and return to technical striking. I lean Yan by decision again. --Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

stories.headline: 'No regrets': why Kangaroos prop made switch from Tonga
stories.summary: Keaon Koloamatangi has revealed why he couldn't knock back the opportunity to represent Australia at the World Cup after previously doing the same with Tonga.
stories.body:
Keaon Koloamatangi has revealed why he couldn't knock back the opportunity to represent Australia at the World Cup after previously doing the same with Tonga.

In recent years, the international scene has mostly showcased players with multiple heritages moving across from tier-one sides such as New Zealand and Australia to play for nations such as Samoa and Tonga in particular.

Koloamatangi went the other way, switching from Tonga to Australia before last year's Ashes tour after previously representing the Mate Ma'a on 10 occasions, including the 2022 World Cup.

"I just want to experience everything. I was lucky enough to play for Tonga in the last World Cup in England," Koloamatangi said

"I think if Australia comes calling, it's not something you can turn your back on. It's probably the best team you can make, and it's something I want to look back on, knowing I always dreamt of doing it as a kid."

Koloamatangi, who will join St George Illawarra next season from South Sydney, has a deep appreciation for both nations and does not regard his choice this time as valuing one side of his heritage over the other.

The 28-year-old will play prop against Fiji at Suncorp Stadium on Sunday night as a proud Kangaroo.

"I played for Tonga, I've play Origin, and I wanted to play for all the nations that I am eligible for," he said.

"It's something I'm really proud of because I'm just as Australian as I am Tongan. I was born Australian and my dad's Tongan. For me, I just wanted to experience a World Cup in the Australian colours, and I've got a lot of great mates here too."

Koloamatangi admits it was "a tough decision" but the classy response of Tonga coach Kristian Woolf reassured him.

"I spoke to Woolfy and he was very grateful for the conversation I had with him. He was respectful and accepted my decision. I have no regrets," Koloamatangi said.

"I loved my time with Tonga, with the atmosphere they get and the crowds they get.

"They're such a small country, and seeing them on the big stage now I've been being blessed to be a part of it."

There is a chance Tonga and Australia could meet in the World Cup semi-final or final.

Tonga's 30-12 win over England in the opening round has them on track to reach the final-four.

"I watched the game last week and was so proud of how they turned up for their nation," Koloamatangi said.

"Obviously, I want Australia to win, but if we weren't to win, I'll be cheering the Tongans all the way. I wish nothing but the best for them."

stories.headline: How Kimi Antonelli can win F1 title at United States GP -- with or without Qatar, Abu Dhabi races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli, it's too late

- Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant Singapore drive

- Hamilton calls Singapore strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: St. Louis GK Bürki stretchered off after collision in Open Cup final
stories.summary: St. Louis goalkeeper Roman Bürki was taken to the hospital after taking a knock to the head during the U.S. Open Cup final against the Columbus Crew.
stories.body:
St. Louis City goalkeeper Roman Bürki was taken to the hospital after taking a knock to the head in a collision during his team's U.S. Open Cup final win over the Columbus Crew on Wednesday night.

In an attempt to make a save in the 70th minute, Bürki took a knee to the head from Crew winger Anass Zaroury. He remained on the ground to receive medical attention before being stretchered off the field.

Bürki was able to wave to supporters as he was taken away from the pitch. St. Louis confirmed to ESPN that Bürki was conscious and moving all extremities on his way to the hospital.

"He is currently alert and in good spirits. The club's medical staff will continue to monitor his condition and the team will provide additional updates as they become available," the club later said in a statement on X.

The score was tied 0-0 at the time of the injury, but St. Louis went on to win the game in a shootout after Burki's backup Ben Lundt made a save to help his team beat the Crew 5-3 on spot kicks.

The win earned St. Louis, which began play in MLS in 2023, its first trophy in club history.

St. Louis City captain Bürki had 43 touches and three crucial saves before the injury. He played an integral role in maintaining the 0-0 draw before being replaced by Lundt after the head injury.

Bürki, who joined St. Louis from Borussia Dortmund in 2022, stopped a corner kick from Brais Méndez that appeared to be goalbound and a flurry of other shots just before sustaining his injury.

Eleven minutes of injury time was added due to Bürki's injury, but neither team scored before the end of regulation despite Columbus outshooting St. Louis 16-3, so the game went to extra time and penalties.

stories.headline: Who will win the Ballon d'Or? Messi, Yamal, Kane -- or someone else?
stories.summary: There's no consensus pick for this year's Ballon d'Or -- but maybe there should be. Here's who actually deserves to win it.
stories.body:
It's probably going to be Harry Kane or Lamine Yamal -- the 33-year-old or the 19-year-old.

At least, that's what the prediction markets are telling us: Kane currently has about a two-in-three chance of winning the men's Ballon d'Or, Yamal a 28% chance, and then the remaining percentage points get split among Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi.

This is a silly award. You probably don't need me to tell you that, but it bears repeating since it seems as if the players themselves care more about it than ever before.

If you look back at the development of the odds, Messi was the favorite before the World Cup final and then Kane was the favorite after the World Cup final ... even though Kane didn't play in the World Cup final.

Or to put it another way: If Yamal scored a goal in the World Cup final, he'd probably be the heavy favorite to win the award. He took four shots, more than anyone in the match, but since none of them went in, it means he might not actually be the best soccer player in the world.

OK, fine, this award isn't necessarily trying to identify the best player in the world. Well, it is -- but it also isn't.

Among the Ballon d'Or regulations, Article 2 reads: "The Ballon d'Or rewards the best male and female player in the world, regardless of league or nationality."

But then Article 4 says: "The Ballon d'Or is awarded based on three criteria, in order of importance: 1. Individual performances, decisive and impressive character. 2. Collective performances and titles won. 3. Class and fair play."

So, it goes to the best player regardless of league or nationality -- but one of the main criteria is team performance, which rewards players who play on the best teams and were born in the right countries?

It makes no sense, which makes it easy to make just about any argument. In a way, everyone is right.

But let's just say this thing worked like the most valuable player award in American sports. If it did, which man should be getting the trophy at Monday's awards ceremony?

Who does conventional wisdom say should win?
To get a somewhat objective, general sense of how the season went, let's first take a look at the European Sports Media Team of the Month. Since 1995, a group of journalists have voted on a starting 11 of the best players on the continent every month. They've given us a consistent, historical database for perceived performance at every position across the top leagues in the world.

Messi made 88 teams of the month, Cristiano Ronaldo is second with 51, and no one else has more than 34. That's a pretty good summation of the state of play since 1995, is it not?

Among currently active players in Europe, Napoli's Kevin De Bruyne (32 appearances) and Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk (30) rank fourth and sixth all time -- and they're the only current Europe-based players to hit 30. The next closest is Real Madrid's Mbappé with 25.

Here's who led the way in Team of the Month appearances last season:

1) Harry Kane: 8

2) David Raya: 7

T-3) Gabriel Magalhães, Declan Rice and Michael Olise: 6

6) Kylian Mbappé: 5

T-7) Erling Haaland and Achraf Hakimi: 4

The most interesting name there is Raya, who didn't even make the 30-team Ballon d'Or shortlist. (In fact, no goalkeepers made the shortlist.) Raya failed to make the Team of the Month only twice, in January and February.

January went to Anatoliy Trubin, who scored -- yes, scored -- the spectacular last-second goal against Real Madrid to qualify Benfica for the knockout rounds of the Champions League. And then February went to Manchester City's Gianluigi Donnarumma, who led all goalkeepers with two TOTM appearances the season before.

The most interesting name not there is Raya's international teammate, Yamal. He made only two Teams of the Month -- fewer than Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly, PSG's Vitinha and Nuno Mendes, Bayern Munich's Joshua Kimmich and Arsenal's William Saliba.

Then, of course, we have the World Cup. One simple, imperfect way of looking at that tournament in a similar way is to see how many Man of the Match awards a given player won. It's close to impossible for a defender to win one, unless they score a goal. But like I said: imperfect!

The leaders:

1) Lionel Messi: 5

2) Jude Bellingham: 4

T-3) Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland and Vinícius Júnior: 3

Kane and Yamal (and Ronaldo, huh?, and a bunch of others) each won two. Olise and Hakimi nabbed one. Raya didn't play a single minute in the tournament, and Magalhães and Rice both left with zero.

Who was actually the best soccer player in the 2025-26 season?
We'll start with the simple numbers: goals+assists. We're looking at total production, not per-90 performance, since every game counts unlike in American sports.

Across Europe's Big Five top leagues, the Champions League and the World Cup, who had the most goals+assists? Here's the top 10:

There's a clear top two, but as we went over last year: goals+assists still doesn't tell us everything we want to know. Assists are just passes that another guy converted into a goal, and not all goals are created equal.

So, we can look at expected assists, a measure of the quality of the passes a player is making -- regardless of what the guy on the end of the pass does. And we can adjust the goals number to account for penalties -- the average penalty is converted 79% of the time, so rather than rewarding the player for being chosen to take the penalty, we'll give them 21% of a goal for each penalty they scored.

The list now looks like this:

Kane and Mbappé are essentially equal, and Olise and Haaland have both also closed the gap to the top. Here, I'd also like to point out that Messi ranks 139th on this list -- above Rafael Leão and just slightly below Christian Pulisic -- despite the numbers only counting his eight matches from the World Cup.

Of course, scoring and creating chances isn't the only thing a soccer player does. The newest widespread advanced metric -- possession value -- looks at how much each action a player takes on the ball increases or decreases his team's chances of scoring a goal. If we swap that in for expected assists, then here's how our top 10 looks:

So, while the adjustments brought everything closer together, there's a clear top two in attacking production -- Kane and Mbappé -- followed by Olise and Haaland in a tier right behind. And then there's another tier with Vinicius Junior, Yamal, and Luis Díaz.

Should that be what the final ballot looks like?

My ballot for the 2026 Ballon d'Or
This is by no means a clean or even an analytically sound analysis. Most of the numbers come from models, and models are, well, models of reality, not objective truth. Even minor-seeming changes in what your expected-possession value is estimating -- is it probability of a goal in the next 10 seconds; by the end of the possession; within the next 10 touches? -- can drastically change the end results.

Still, models like the xPV from Stats Perform do something we can't: watch and contextualize every single touch a player takes across an entire year. And when you do that, there's a clear group of players who stand out: Kane, Mbappé, Haaland and Olise.

That tracks nicely with the media voting from throughout the season: They were the four attackers with the most Team of the Month appearances.

But what about the likes of Raya, Rice, Magalhães and Hakimi?

Raya, I think, benefits from being the backstop for the best defense we've seen in a long time. He's very good, but he's not saving so many shots more than you'd expect that you could argue he's providing as much value as any of these attackers.

Rice is the best midfielder in the world, but he's not so much better than No. 2 that he should vault over a superstar attacker. A relatively muted World Cup didn't help, either.

Magalhães winning wouldn't feel right; most would agree that he's not even the best center back on his own team. (That'd be William Saliba.) And Hakimi is the best fullback in the world, but he didn't have the kind of outlier season he had the year before.

So, who should win? All four of the players mentioned above would be worthy winners. And I'd extend it out to five options.

At this exact moment, Yamal is the best player in the world -- in my opinion -- but even if you adjust for the difficulty of the leagues, then his production over the 2025-26 season still trails Olise, and they play the same position. I wouldn't give it to him, but Messi was the best player at the World Cup and seems as if he might actually be the best player in the world -- still. He's going to get first-place votes.

If we account for league difficulty, then Mbappé had the best season by my made-up adjusted goals+xPV number -- by a significant margin. LaLiga is the second-best league in the world, he racked up numbers in the Champions League and the World Cup, and he adds extra value in possession in a way that neither Kane nor Haaland do. His xPV was more than Kane and Haaland combined.

Olise, meanwhile, led all players in xPV while rarely turning the ball over and pressing aggressively. Mbappé, of course, barely even presses anymore. On top of that, Real Madrid have been a worse team since he joined, and PSG got better as soon as he left.

The main thing that's holding me back from picking Olise is that he didn't score at the World Cup. He was second on France with around 2.5 expected goals, and there's nothing to suggest he's a bad finisher anywhere else in his career, but ... you've got to put the ball into the net to actually realize the value you're creating by getting the shot in the first place. He could've easily scored four goals from those shots, and if he did? Then I'm putting him at No. 1.

That seems silly, but I really think that's how slim the margins are among this top group of players. I also haven't really mentioned anyone on PSG -- they're all hurt by the fact that they barely play any minutes in Ligue 1. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, in particular, was second behind Mbappé for the goals+xPV number in the Champions League. He presses, he doesn't lose the ball, and he gets dinged because he played so few league minutes and because he's from a tiny country that didn't qualify for the World Cup.

All of which leads me to my No. 1 pick, who gives us something close to the best of all worlds: a goal scorer who isn't a complete zero on the defensive end and who contributes in buildup play.

He's someone who was great in domestic league play, great in the Champions League, and great in the World Cup. And although he plays for a financially dominant team in an uncompetitive league, his knocked out Real Madrid in the quarters and nearly knocked off PSG in the semifinals.

Here, then, is what the top 10 of my ballot would look like:

1) Harry Kane, Bayern Munich

2) Michael Olise, Bayern Munich

3) Lamine Yamal, Barcelona

4) Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid

5) Erling Haaland, Manchester City

6) Declan Rice, Arsenal

7) Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, PSG

8) Gabriel Magalhães, Arsenal

9) Lionel Messi, Inter Miami

10) Julián Álvarez, Atletico Madrid

stories.headline: Maxey, Sixers turn Philly boos into cheers in 29-point comeback over Cavaliers
stories.summary: Booed after trailing by 24 at the half, the Sixers rode a game-high 32 points from Tyrese Maxey to erase a 29-point deficit and stun the Cavs 114-106 on Thursday.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The crowd at Xfinity Arena watched the Sixers cut a 29-point deficit to 10 in the third quarter Thursday night when Tyrese Maxey caught a pass from LeBron James in transition and, without taking a dribble, launched a 3-pointer.

As the ball went through the net, forcing the Cavs to call a timeout, Maxey walked toward the fans behind the scorers' table and screamed as Jaylen Brown flanked him in celebration and Joel Embiid celebrated on the other end of the court.

On a team laden with stars, Maxey was the conductor of this raucous Philadelphia crowd, which followed his lead all night as the Sixers roared back to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106.

The 29-point comeback was the Cavaliers' largest blown lead and the Sixers' largest comeback in the play-by-play era. It was also the largest comeback of James' 24-year career.

"It was just a great moment," said Maxey, who led all scorers with 32 points and added six assists. "The crowd was into the game. We were just feeding off the crowd, feeding off our energy, feeding off our resilience."

Two nights after their season-opening win over the reigning champion New York Knicks, the Sixers were outclassed in nearly every way to begin Thursday night's game. They turned the ball over, couldn't get stops and missed layups.

Brown had just four points in his lowest-scoring first half at home since March 2025, while the Sixers' 15 first-half turnovers were their most in a half since January 2024. The Cavs' 69-45 halftime lead tied their largest in a season-opening half in franchise history and matched their largest halftime lead over the 76ers in franchise history.

As the first half ended, the crowd, most wearing the white opening night shirts with the Sixers roster and coach Nick Nurse printed on them, loudly booed.

Maxey said he challenged his teammates during the intermission.

"I said, 'Well, it's time to see what we made of. Are we going to be some front-runners and only be happy when stuff is good? Or when stuff is bad, are we going to fight and be resilient?' And we did that," Maxey said.

The Sixers responded with a quarter that Brown said "shifted the game," coming out of the break on an 8-0 run and outscoring Cleveland 37-21 in the third quarter.

Still, the Sixers went into the fourth trailing by eight. It wasn't until the 6:54 mark that they took the lead, when Embiid hit a 16-foot jump shot over center Jarrett Allen that gave Philadelphia a lead it wouldn't relinquish.

Embiid said the team's resilience Thursday night was different from past teams he has been a part of during his 11-year Sixers career.

"No shade to anybody that's been here, but in the past, a lot of people would've just laid down and tried to move on to the next one," Embiid said.

He added: "Yeah, it was different. I said last game, after the game, it just feels different."

The Sixers were a different team in the second half Thursday night, turning the ball over only twice compared with 15 times for the Cavs.

Nurse said the Sixers also struggled in the first half defending the Cavaliers' mid-pick-and-roll plays. According to GeniusIQ, in the first half, Cleveland ran 27 direct picks and averaged 1.08 points on them. In the second half, the Cavaliers ran 20 direct picks and averaged only 0.56 points. Nurse shifted the team's defensive assignments, and it worked.

The Cavs scored just 37 points in the second half. Guard Donovan Mitchell, who had 30 points through three quarters, was held to just two points in the fourth, and those came with the game out of reach.

"They were just way, way, way tougher than us in the first half," Maxey said. "They were just punking us honestly, and we did a good job of playing back second."

Still, James said the Sixers can't expect to have comeback performances like that regularly.

"You don't want to rely on that," James said, laughing. "I think it's great to know deep down we're not going to have that quit mentality ... but you don't want to put yourself in too many of those situations."

During the Sixers' comeback, the crowd's boos turned into raucous cheers. Embiid called it a "top-three" night in his career, while guard VJ Edgecombe said it was the best atmosphere he has played in as a pro. James called Philadelphia "one of the best sports cities."

"I've been here for a long time. ... I have no words," Embiid said. "That was amazing."

stories.headline: Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'
stories.summary: Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.
stories.body:
Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.

Fernandes followed Martínez in producing an eye-catching post-match interview on the back of Wednesday's 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League.

The result increased the scrutiny on Michael Carrick, who then faced criticism from Fernandes for the game plan in Italy but Rooney has accused the current United captain and Martínez -- who pointed the finger at Jason Wilcox -- of being selfish.

Sources: Carrick to lead Man United against Bournemouth

During an appearance on "The United Stand" podcast, Rooney, who also called for the board to provide clarity regarding Carrick's future, said: "When Martínez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart. That was the start.

"We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players. The reason why is because them players don't want to take responsibility.

"You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said, but you have to take responsibility on the pitch, you have to take responsibility as a group of players and there were times when me and Sir Alex Ferguson wouldn't talk, but I'd run through a brick wall for him on the pitch.

"These players, they're selfish. They care about themselves, they don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, about the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

"If they're not getting what's right for them. They're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves. They have to look at themselves.

- Ogden: Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Dawson: Man United were abysmal in Como, but only Carrick who will suffer

"Bruno, he's having probably the worst run of form he's had since he's been at the club and again, it's no coincidence he's putting pressure on someone else because he doesn't want to face it.

"If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martínez looks at himself in the mirror, all the players... they'll find what is looking back at them is them and it's not good enough."

stories.headline: Caleb Williams throws 2 TD passes as the Bears beat Drake Maye and the Patriots 30-24
stories.summary: — Round 2 went to Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- — Round 2 went to Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears.


Williams passed for 308 yards and two touchdowns, and the Bears cooled off Drake Maye and the New England Patriots with a 30-24 victory Thursday night.


It was the second meeting between the young quarterbacks since they were part of the 2024 NFL draft. Maye, who was selected by New England at No. 3, directed the Patriots to a 19-3 victory over Williams and the Bears when the longtime friends were rookies.


But Williams, the No. 1 overall pick, leaned on Luther Burden and Colston Loveland while outlasting Maye and the Patriots in the rematch. Williams connected on 22 of 33 passes in his second game back after being sidelined by a right hamstring injury.


“These nights are awesome,” Williams said. “You play against another good team on a primetime game in a short week, these games are awesome because you get to see who you are as a team. That’s who we are. We’re a smashmouth football team, an innovative team. And when things happen and things don’t go our way and the water is rocky, we stay steady.”


Maye was 24 for 31 for 321 yards and two touchdowns. He also had a 7-yard run for New England's first TD with 11:33 left in the first half.


But Maye also was intercepted by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson in the end zone on a pass intended for rookie tight end Eli Raridon late in the second quarter.


“It’s those plays, I talk about it all the time,” Maye said. “You know those plays that can swing the game, can impact the game and that was definitely one of them right there. Yeah, I wish I definitely had that one back.”


New England (4-3) had won three consecutive games behind Maye, who threw 10 TD passes and one interception during the win streak.


“He gave us a chance," Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said. "He competed and I know he’d like to have that throw back to Eli, but I thought he really competed. Whether that was running around and scrambling or finding good places to go with the football. He gave us a chance. ... I’m glad he’s ours.”


Burden had four catches for 130 yards for Chicago (5-2), and Loveland had a 12-yard touchdown reception. Cairo Santos kicked a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left, a career long and matching the franchise record, after he missed a 53-yard attempt earlier in the final quarter.


Williams became the first Bears quarterback to throw for more than 300 yards in consecutive games since Mitch Trubisky had a three-game run in 2018.


“I think he did a pretty good job throughout the night,” Bears coach Ben Johnson said. “I know he had a number of explosive plays. He found some of those guys at the second level that were huge for us.”


After Santos’ long field goal, Maye drove New England into range for Andy Borregales’ 47-yarder with 37 seconds to go. But Chicago recovered the ensuing onside kick.


Rhamondre Stevenson had five catches for 93 yards and a touchdown for the Patriots. Raridon had a 30-yard TD catch in the third quarter.


“We did some good things,” Vrabel said. “But again, didn’t do enough.”


It was Chicago’s first home game since Mike Ditka died on Oct. 9. The Bears saluted the Hall of Fame tight end and longtime coach with a pregame moment of silence, and they also handed out fake mustaches to the crowd of 60,520 at Soldier Field.


Ditka’s No. 89 jersey dotted the stands, and fans also donned Bears sweaters in a callback to what he wore on the sideline as a coach.


Chicago opened a 20-7 lead on Burden’s 24-yard touchdown with 14 seconds left in the first half. Burden got the ball on a screen on third-and-17, and Loveland, Kalif Raymond and Darnell Wright helped clear the way for his second TD reception of the season.


“The whole calvary came ... and it was like a wave carrying him through there,” Johnson said. “He saw a little crease and hit the jets.”


Set to receive the second-half kickoff, the Bears were in position to pull away. But the Patriots responded with Stevenson’s 48-yard touchdown reception on the final play of the period.


Stevenson slipped out of the backfield and Maye lobbed the ball over the head of Bears safety Cam Lewis. Stevenson ran away from Lewis and got a downfield block from DeMario Douglas before cutting past Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson on his way to the end zone.


Injuries
Patriots: CB Christian Gonzalez played after being listed as questionable because of an illness. ... S Kevin Byard departed after he was checked out by trainers with 9:44 left in first half. He later returned. ... DT Christian Barmore departed late in the game.


Bears: CB Malik Muhammad left in the third quarter with a toe injury. ... TE Cole Kmet hurt his right knee on a reception with 5:34 left. "We’ll know more tomorrow, but I don’t think it looked very good,” Johnson said.


Up next
Patriots: At Miami on Nov. 1.


Bears: At Seattle for a Monday night game Nov. 2.
